items.title: UAV Systems Engineer / Business Development Engineer (Part-time)
bullets: Built the business strategy and technical validation plan for an autonomy initiative (underground mining), covering competitive benchmarking, use case definition and presentations to senior stakeholders
Led business development for the docking station line, turning CAPEX and OPEX per station into payback and margin curves that set pricing and go-to-market direction
Led the company presence at LEAP 2026, lifting booth engagement 35% and securing 2 new POC agreements
Owned the mechanical design of the docking station from requirements to working prototype, coordinating suppliers and design reviews
Worked on GPS-denied LiDAR SLAM for underground mining drones: benchmarked approaches (KISS-ICP, Gazebo) and wrote a test plan across five simulation modules
Designed a universal GCS enclosure: IP65 case, LiFePO4 power, thermal management and FEA-checked retention hardware; passive charging funnel CAD for the docking station
Produced the GCS engineering document including link verification; booth and pitch materials aimed at government buyers
items.notes: LEAP 2026 figures (35% engagement, 2 POC agreements) are self-reported on your CV. Be ready to explain how engagement was measured.

Pitch the service to employers so their employees can benefit from it

items.title: UAV Engineering Intern
bullets: Designed a fixed-wing platform from a clean sheet, carrying it from concept through detailed design to build
Owned the full bill of materials, selecting propulsion, avionics and structural components against cost and performance targets
Released 45+ part drawings in SolidWorks; took the airframe from CAD to 3D-printed parts with CNC and laser cutting along the way
Set up Mission Planner and flight parameters for the lab's platforms
Presented the drones department and its platforms to visiting delegations and investors
Offered an extended internship and a role after it (per portfolio)

items.title: MEP Site Engineer Intern
bullets: Coordinated multidisciplinary site crews of 15+ tradesmen against daily targets on an active construction site
Reviewed 11+ engineering drawings across HVAC, plumbing and firefighting scopes and resolved clashes with contractors
Found and resolved 8 first-floor clashes (4 HVAC, 4 plumbing) and presented them with fixes to the project team
HVAC fixes: lowered a cable tray, resized the stair exhaust duct, reshaped a supply duct to clear a drop panel, rerouted fire branch lines around VRF units with paired 45 degree elbows
Plumbing fixes: moved 110, 76 and 50 mm mains from offices into corridors, dropped them under the AC duct, fixed a shower drain with a core opening
Oversaw on-site installations and enforced HSE requirements, working to a zero-incident standard
Proposed one shared schedule for electrical, mechanical and fire teams
items.notes: Evidence supports HVAC/plumbing/fire coordination, drawing review and clash resolution. It does not show that you designed complete HVAC systems.

items.title: NavPod: GPS-denied navigation pod for fixed-wing UAV (Founder & Team Lead)
bullets: Originated the concept and led a multidisciplinary team to 2nd place nationally (university track), 15,000 SAR prize
Built a MATLAB/Simulink model from scratch: 12-state 6-DOF BWB dynamics with elevon mixing, a 15-state EKF and L1 guidance
Defined the two-loop architecture separating AI mission processing (Jetson Orin Nano, ORB-SLAM3, YOLOv8) from flight stabilization (Pixhawk / ArduPilot) over MAVLink
Designed the pod in SolidWorks (240 mm, 75 mm diameter), ran CFD (SimScale) and owned the 575 g mass budget
Built a WebGL mission simulation used live at the final; featured in Saudi News coverage
Continuing as ApexNav for SAIF: terrain navigation, AI-aided INS drift correction, hardware-in-the-loop sim
